newsitem.title: INDIA: Leader of Indian PM's party faces prosecution -PTI.
newsitem.headline: Leader of Indian PM's party faces prosecution -PTI.

text.p: An Indian state governor on Tuesday authorised federal police to prosecute the leader of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's party in a $280-million corruption scandal, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.

The governor of the eastern state of Bihar authorised the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to pursue legal proceedings against the state's chief minister, Laloo Prasad Yadav, in a "fodder" scandal, the news agency said.
CBI and Bihar state officials including Yadav could not be reached for comment.
Yadav, who heads Gujral's Janata Dal party, has said he is innocent in the scandal which dates back to the 1980s and involved the alleged siphoning off of animal welfare funds.
The largest component of the 15-party ruling United Front coalition, the Janata Dal has been divided by the scandal and a bitter internal squabble to elect a new party chief.

Yadav has resisted pressure from party colleagues to step down as Bihar chief minister, and is pitted against the party's working president, Sharad Yadav, in internal elections that the party wants to hold soon.
Sharad Yadav is no relation to the Bihar chief minister.

The struggle between the two contenders has spilled over into the courts, which have issued a string of rulings on the party elections. On Tuesday, a Delhi court authorised the party's national executive to fix the date and venue of the polls.
PTI said Bihar governor A.R. Kidwai had also authorised the CBI to prosecute two other state ministers as well as a former state chief from the Congress party.
Gujral's communist partners in the United Front as well as some Janata Dal members have pressed for Laloo Prasad Yadav's resignation, but he has resisted.
"This will affect the Janata Dal and the ripples are bound to be there on the coalition," a senior United Front leader who asked not to be identified told Reuters.
The scandal broke last year when officials discovered large withdrawals from animal welfare accounts.
The CBI had required permission from the state governor to prosecute Yadav, who is among 55 officials and politicians named by the federal police in connection with the scandal.
